title: Sennacherib’s sons escaped into “the land of Armenia” — the Hebrew prints “the land of Ararat”
summary: In both 2 Kings 19:37 and Isaiah 37:38 the KJV says Adrammelech and Sharezer escaped “into the land of Armenia”. The Hebrew prints אֶרֶץ אֲרָרָט, “the land of Ararat”, a different name, and Brenton’s Greek prints Ararath.
text: KJV 2 Kings 19:37: “And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Armenia. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 19:37: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית ׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר (בָּנָיו֙  ק) הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃  פ [and it happened, as he was bowing down in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him with the sword, and they escaped to the land of Ararat; and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 19:37: Καὶ ἐγένετο αὐτοῦ προσκυνοῦντος ἐν οἴκῳ Μεσερὰχ τοῦ θεοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ Ἀδραμέλεχ καὶ Σαρασὰρ οἱ υἱοὶ αὐτοῦ ἐπάταξαν αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρᾳ· καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐσώθησαν εἰς γῆν Ἀραράθ· καὶ ἐβασίλευσεν Ἀσορδὰν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ ἀντʼ αὐτοῦ. KJV Isaiah 37:38: “And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword; and they escaped into the land of Armenia: and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.” Hebrew (WLC) Isaiah 37:38: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא  מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית ׀ נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר בָּנָיו֙ הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר־חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנֹ֖ו תַּחְתָּֽיו׃    ס Brenton English 2 Kings 19:37: “And it came to pass, while he was worshipping in the house of Meserach his god, that Adramelech and Sarasar his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Ararath; and Asordan his son reigned in his stead.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI19.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/19/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI19.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI19.htm, https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/ISA37.htm and https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/23/37/.
reasoning: The KJV puts the later regional name “Armenia” where both Hebrew verses print the name אֲרָרָט (Ararat), with אֶרֶץ, “land”. The Hebrew text has no word that reads “Armenia”; the Septuagint transliterates Ararath, as the Hebrew does. A reader of the KJV alone does not see that the verse names Ararat, the name the KJV prints in Genesis 8:4 for the mountains where the ark rested.

The two names may point to the same region: the KJV’s “Armenia” can be a modern-for-ancient substitution, and this record does not say the KJV places the sons in the wrong country or that Ararat and Armenia are different places. title: An ass’s head at “fourscore pieces of silver” — Brenton’s Greek says fifty
summary: During the siege of Samaria the KJV says an ass’s head sold for “fourscore pieces of silver”. The Hebrew prints בִּשְׁמֹנִים כֶּסֶף, eighty of silver; Brenton’s Greek prints πεντήκοντα ἀργυρίου, fifty of silver. The price of the dove’s dung, five pieces, agrees.
text: KJV 2 Kings 6:25: “And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 6:25: וַיְהִ֨י רָעָ֤ב גָּדֹול֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְרֹ֔ון וְהִנֵּ֖ה צָרִ֣ים עָלֶ֑יהָ עַ֣ד הֱיֹ֤ות רֹאשׁ־חֲמֹור֙ בִּשְׁמֹנִ֣ים כֶּ֔סֶף וְרֹ֛בַע הַקַּ֥ב [חֲרֵייֹונִים כ] (דִּבְיֹונִ֖ים  ק) בַּחֲמִשָּׁה־כָֽסֶף׃ [and there was a great famine in Samaria, and behold, besieging it, until the head of a donkey was at eighty of silver, and the fourth of a qab of dove’s dung/pods at five of silver]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 6:25: Καὶ ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐν Σαμαρείᾳ· καὶ ἰδοὺ περιεκάθηντο ἐπʼ αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἐγενήθη κεφαλὴ ὄνου πεντήκοντα ἀργυρίου, καὶ τέταρτον τοῦ κάβου κόπρου περιστερῶν πέντε ἀργυρίου. [… until the head of a donkey was fifty of silver, and a fourth of a qab of doves’ dung five of silver]. Brenton English: “And there was a great famine in Samaria: and, behold, they besieged it, until an ass's head was valued at fifty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove's dung at five pieces of silver.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI06.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/6/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI06.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI06.htm.
reasoning: The KJV’s “fourscore” is eighty and matches the Hebrew word שְׁמֹנִים. Brenton’s Greek has the word for fifty. The two texts print different numbers for the same price in the same verse, so a reader who follows the Greek tradition reads a cheaper head than a reader of the Hebrew.

The Hebrew marks the word for the second item with a written form and a read form (חֲרֵייֹונִים, דִּבְיֹונִים); that is not the point of this record and is not compared. title: “full ears of corn in the husk thereof” — Brenton’s Greek has “cakes of figs”
summary: The man from Baalshalisha brings Elisha twenty barley loaves and, in the KJV, “full ears of corn in the husk thereof”. The Hebrew word beside the loaves is וְכַרְמֶל בְּצִקְלֹנוֹ; Brenton’s Greek prints καὶ παλάθας, “and cakes of figs”, and has nothing like “in the husk”.
text: KJV 2 Kings 4:42: “And there came a man from Baalshalisha, and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and full ears of corn in the husk thereof. And he said, Give unto the people, that they may eat.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 4:42: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנֹ֑ו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃ [and a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought to the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and karmel in his bag/sack; and he said, Give to the people and let them eat]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 4:42: Καὶ ἀνὴρ διῆλθεν ἐκ Βαιθαρισὰ, καὶ ἤνεγκε πρὸς τὸν ἄνθρωπον τοῦ Θεοῦ πρωτογεννημάτων εἴκοσι ἄρτους κριθίνους καὶ παλάθας· καὶ εἶπε, δότε τῷ λαῷ καὶ ἐσθιέτωσαν. Brenton English: “And there came a man over from Bætharisa, and brought to the man of God twenty barley loaves and cakes of figs, of the first-fruits. And he said, Give to the people, and let them eat.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI04.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/4/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI04.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI04.htm.
reasoning: The KJV renders the Hebrew words כרמל בצקלנו as a grain, “full ears of corn”, with “in the husk thereof” for the following word. Brenton’s Greek names a different food, παλάθας (pressed cakes, here “cakes of figs”), and does not render the Hebrew phrase that the KJV renders “in the husk”. Each text lists a second item beside the barley loaves, but they name different things.
scope: T applies at 2 Kings 4:42, Septuagint only. The record does not decide the meaning of the Hebrew words כַּרְמֶל and צִקְלֹן, which the KJV and the Greek take differently; it claims no Hebrew mistranslation and does not say which food was brought. title: The scouts sent after the Syrians: “two chariot horses” — Brenton’s Greek says two horsemen
summary: In the KJV the king’s servants take “two chariot horses” and send them after the Syrian army. Brenton’s Greek prints δύο ἐπιβάτας ἵππων, “two horsemen”, riders on horses, where the KJV has animals drawing a chariot.
text: KJV 2 Kings 7:14: “They took therefore two chariot horses; and the king sent after the host of the Syrians, saying, Go and see.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 7:14: וַיִּקְח֕וּ שְׁנֵ֖י רֶ֣כֶב סוּסִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אַחֲרֵ֧י מַחֲנֵֽה־אֲרָ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר לְכ֥וּ וּרְאֽוּ׃ [and they took two of chariot of horses, and the king sent after the camp of Aram, saying, Go and see]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 7:14: Καὶ ἔλαβον δύο ἐπιβάτας ἵππων· καὶ ἀπέστειλεν ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ ὀπίσω τοῦ βασιλέως Συρίας, λέγων, δεῦτε, καὶ ἴδετε. Brenton English: “So they took two horsemen; and the king of Israel sent after the king of Syria, saying, Go, and see.” Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/2KI07.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/12/7/, https://ebible.org/grcbrent/2KI07.htm and https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/2KI07.htm.
reasoning: The KJV’s “two chariot horses” follows the Hebrew שְׁנֵי רֶכֶב סוּסִים, which has the word רֶכֶב (chariotry, chariot) and the word for horses. title: Manasseh “made his son pass through the fire” (Kings) — “his children” (Chronicles); the Greek of Kings has sons
summary: 2 Kings 21:6 says Manasseh made “his son” pass through the fire, one person in the Hebrew (בְּנוֹ). 2 Chronicles 33:6 says “his children” (בָּנָיו), in the valley of the son of Hinnom. Brenton’s Greek of 2 Kings 21:6 prints the plural τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ, “his sons”.
text: KJV 2 Kings 21:6: “And he made his son pass through the fire, and observed times, and used enchantments, and dealt with familiar spirits and wizards: he wrought much wickedness in the sight of the Lord, to provoke him to anger.” Hebrew (WLC) 2 Kings 21:6: וְהֶעֱבִ֤יר אֶת־בְּנֹו֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וְעֹונֵ֣ן וְנִחֵ֔שׁ וְעָ֥שָׂה אֹ֖וב וְיִדְּעֹנִ֑ים הִרְבָּ֗ה לַעֲשֹׂ֥ות הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה לְהַכְעִֽיס׃ [and he made his son pass through the fire, and practised soothsaying and divination, and made a ghost-spirit and wizards, and did much evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke him to anger]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 2 Kings 21:6: Καὶ διῆγε τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐν πυρί, καὶ ἐκληδονίζετο καὶ οἰωνίζετο, καὶ ἐποίησε τεμένη, καὶ γνώστας ἐπλήθυνε τοῦ ποιεῖν τὸ πονηρὸν ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς Κυρίου παροργίσαι αὐτόν.
